mechanism_claims.claim_text: KDEON WK-11 directly perturbs microbial membranes in the Sytox Green assay; this supports membrane permeabilization as a direct mechanism for the tested organisms.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source describes organism-specific kinetics; exact fluorescence values are figure-level and are not normalized into numeric database rows here.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KDEON WK-11 shows direct bactericidal/viability effects by CFU recovery assays and killing kinetics.
direct_assay_types: P. aeruginosa killing kinetics in PBS
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KDEON WK-11 against representative microbial strains
mechanism_claims.limitations: CFU plots support killing phenotypes; exact plotted point extraction was not needed for row-level database conflict resolution.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KDEON WK-11 binds lipid A/LPS-related material in ESI-MS experiments, supporting anti-LPS interaction as a direct binding mechanism.
direct_assay_types: Electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry lipid A binding
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KDEON WK-11 with diphosphorylated lipid A
mechanism_claims.limitations: Anti-sepsis activity remains proposed/future-facing; the direct source-supported claim is lipid A binding, not in vivo anti-sepsis efficacy.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Predicted LPS-bound alpha-helical/amphipathic structure supports, but does not by itself prove, the membrane insertion model.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Prediction is kept below direct_mechanism strength unless paired with direct Sytox/ESI-MS evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Biofilm metabolic activity, biomass, and pyoverdine assays support antibiofilm/anti-virulence phenotypes for P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KDEON WK-11 against P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 biofilm models
mechanism_claims.limitations: These are activity phenotypes and are not overpromoted to a molecular mechanism beyond source-supported assay type.

mechanism_quality_control.overclaim_guard: Anti-sepsis and LPS-neutralization are kept as bounded/proposed implications unless directly supported by lipid A binding evidence.
